abstract: Maintains drilling permits, watershed utility coordination, and co-funding subsidies
system_message:
You are the Municipal watershed controller (WSH). Your operational responsibilities include maintaining drilling permits, managing watershed utility coordination, administering shared municipal co-funding subsidies, and tracking aquifer recharge flow surveillance across investigative protocol proposals.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains drilling permits, watershed utility coordination, and co-funding subsidies（PERM）
information_points.content:
WSH-PERM-BU4：For Fluorescent dye and particle tracking, municipal watershed drilling authorization is granted with formal drilling exemptions covering proposed exploratory sonic drilling locations within the protected recharge zone, and the shared municipal subsidy deduction provides an offset of 8,000 USD deducted from total project cost through the drinking water protection emergency grant.
WSH-PERM-31P：For Multi-isotope hydrochemical fingerprinting, municipal watershed drilling authorization is granted with formal drilling exemptions for proposed exploratory sonic drilling locations within the protected recharge zone, and the shared municipal subsidy deduction provides a direct municipal cost-share offset of 8,000 USD deducted from total project cost under the drinking water protection emergency grant.
WSH-PERM-D6S：For High-resolution acoustic resistivity profiling, municipal watershed drilling authorization is not granted for the proposed exploratory sonic drilling locations in the protected recharge zone, while the shared municipal subsidy deduction is 8,000 USD deducted from total project cost under the drinking water protection emergency grant.

information_points.title: Aquifer recharge flow surveillance（FLOW）
information_points.content:
WSH-FLOW-FGX：Under Fluorescent dye and particle tracking, monitoring registers a perched aquifer baseflow volume of 210 m3/d as the mean daily effluent discharge rate at the northern recharge boundary weir.
WSH-FLOW-58S：Under Multi-isotope hydrochemical fingerprinting, the perched aquifer baseflow volume is recorded at a mean daily effluent discharge rate of 120 m3/d at the northern recharge boundary weir.
WSH-FLOW-CJ1：Under High-resolution acoustic resistivity profiling, telemetry records indicate a perched aquifer baseflow volume of 160 m3/d measured as the mean daily effluent discharge rate at the northern recharge boundary weir.
